newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK central bank injects HK$598 mln in money market.
newsitem.headline: HK central bank injects HK$598 mln in money market.

text.p: Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the de facto central bank, said it injected HK$598 million into the interbank market on Monday morning in view of the tight liquidity of the local cash market.
"The injection is in response to the tight liquidity of the market," an HKMA executive said.
The money market was especially tight on short-dated cash ahead of the month-end and the implementation of HKMA's Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS).
"Traders are stocking short-term government paper, preparing for the start of the RTGS system on December 9," a dealer said.
Exchange Fund Bills and Notes could be used to secure intraday repurchase (repo) borrowings, which would be interest-free, the dealer said.
Overnight rates eased about 1/4 point while three-month money dipped 1/32 after the injection and closed the morning at 5-1/8 1/16 and 5-17/32 15/32 percent, respectively.
